citations.assessment: The fast and parched-porridge exchange appears in this chapter as cited.
The Lublin text gives Ushparti and explains the name as that of Rav Pappa’s mother.
The located Bavli text identifies Naḥman bar Ushpazti. Heilprin transmits additional wording, so its form remains in translation.
The currently retrieved Ein Yaakov has Rav Natan bar (Oshaya) Ashpazti. Identify the named work without endorsing Heilprin’s distinct reported reading.
Heilprin files this variant under Natan bar Oshaya; the parallel cross-reference does not adjudicate the name in every witness.
Heilprin’s main Rav Pappa entry presents the reported lack of a known father as a possible inference tied to the maternal name.
The Rav Zeira entry cites precisely the idiom and its Rosh Hashanah locus.

holds.raw: והנה היוחסין הבין דרב נחמן הוא בן אושפזתי ולא ר"פ
holds.reason: Heilprin infers Yuḥasin’s interpretation from its placement. The exact Yuḥasin lemma remains to be collated; preserve the inference as Heilprin’s.

holds.raw: רב נחמן בר אושעיה אי שריף מר כו
holds.reason: The retrieved Ein Yaakov uses Natan, with parenthetical Oshaya before Ashpazti. Heilprin’s reported Naḥman bar Oshaya remains an edition-collation item.

holds.raw: ומצינו בפ' במה אשה רב נחמן בר אושעיא
holds.reason: Heilprin cites BaMeh Ishah for the reported form. The precise witness with that reading remains open.

holds.raw: טעה היוחסין במה שהביא רב נחמן בר אושפזתא
holds.reason: The Arukh, Bavli and Ein Yaakov already differ in formulation or names. Retain Heilprin’s judgment of Yuḥasin as a separate voice pending the exact Yuḥasin witness.
